questions.history: Call setAttribute(`k`, A), then setAttribute(`k`, B).
questions.prediction: The parent should bind A then B, omitting A's unbind. The landing should bind A, unbind A, then bind B. After both writes getAttribute(`k`) should be B by identity.
questions.basis: There is one binding under k at a time. The landed overwrite test checks occupancy counters for both listeners.
questions.refutation: The old listener remains bound, the wrong receiver is notified, or the stored object differs from B.

questions.history: Starting empty, bind A once and call removeAttribute(`k`).
questions.prediction: Both revisions should log bind A and unbind A exactly once each. Both events should carry k, the session and A. getAttribute(`k`) should then be null.
questions.basis: The removal path sends the former object to its own listener. The original bind/remove regression observes a zero final counter.
questions.refutation: The lookup stays occupied or either event identifies the wrong name, session or object.

questions.history: On the landing use two distinct listeners that compare equal. Bind A, set A again, then set B. Compare both object identities in the log.
questions.prediction: Only the second call should be silent. Expect bind A, unbind A, bind B and final lookup B.
questions.basis: The same object remains bound on the second write. Equal application values can be distinct lifecycle participants on the third write.
questions.refutation: There is an extra bind for A, or equality suppresses the transition to B.
